agents.name: Claude Code

surface_source.quote: Then, give the thing the list of editing prompts you came up with, and have it run each through the Codex, Claude, or Antigravity CLIs.

agents.quote: In fact, that’s my entire process at this point: I copy a template app directory, open Claude or Codex in it, and tell it what I want to build.

also.quote: I have a standard OpenAI/ChatGPT Pro account; GPT5 is my daily driver for math, and Claude for code.

history.value: Zed agent mode as primary interface
history.quote: I use Zed as my primary interface to "actually doing project work" LLM stuff, because it front-ends both OpenAI and Google/Gemini models, and because I really like the interface.

agents.name: Codex
agents.quote: You want to make sure you’ve got computer-use, or whatever Codex calls it, enabled.

history.value: Codex CLI for casual stuff, starting Codex Web
history.quote: I use Codex CLI for casual stuff, because of the ergonomics of just popping open another terminal tab.
For the last month or so, Gemini 2.5 has been my go-to †.

models.name: GPT-5.5
models.quote: As I said elsewhere: I've fed thousands of math problems through ChatGPT (starting with 4o and now with 5.5).

review_style.value: Agents push PRs, only he merges
review_style.quote: * You may push PRs, but you MUST NOT ever merge them youself to main.

also.quote: If an agent wrote all the SwiftUI code in my project, what do you have to gain from closely reading it?
I have to read the code line-by-line anyways.

harness.value: A spare MacBook running Claude, Makefile builds, never Xcode
harness.quote: I recruited an old Macbook to run Claude on. I set up Xcode and git. I got Claude configured, and tracked down some Swift and macOS design skills.

also.quote: My biggest quality-of-life win is never having to open Xcode. Thankfully, my friend Josh built a purely Makefile-driven build process after trying to compile MDV for himself. I’ve just had Claude copy it to every new project I do.

rules_files.value: CLAUDE.md = AGENTS.md (17 lines), copied into every app
rules_files.quote:
* Record progress in PROGRESS.md. I should be able to tell a future agent "read PLAN.md and
PROGRESS.md" and trust it's up to speed with this codebase.

signature.caption: copied into every new app
signature.why: Our pick: one folder carries his rules, skills and no-Xcode build, so every app starts with cp -R and a sentence.
signature.quote: In fact, that’s my entire process at this point: I copy a template app directory, open Claude or Codex in it, and tell it what I want to build.

archetype.why: Builds personal macOS apps from one reusable template and tells people to write their own agents.

signature_quote.value: AI today is most effective when it's not vibing, but rather copiloting a skilled operator.
signature_quote.more: I don't necessarily want my agent to build an entire system for me, even if it's ultimately the author of almost every line of code; I'm actively making decisions throughout.
